title: Grateful Dead Live at Cafe au Go-Go on 1969-09-29
lineage: AUD > ? > Reel > Cass (Maxell UD w/dolby B, playback on SonyTCK-909ES) > DAT (SV-3700 w/Oade +15dB input gain mod) > ZA2 > DiamondCutNoise Reduction > CD

ai_review.summary: A rare audience‑tape with muddy, vocal‑poor sound that nevertheless captures the legendary “The Seven” jam in all its mind‑blowing glory.
ai_review.review: Despite the cassette’s hiss, missing vocals and a generally thin mix, this recording is treasured for its historic performance – the once‑in‑a‑lifetime full‑band rendition of The Seven, plus a fiery run from Doin’ That Rag into Good Lovin’. Reviewers rave about the jam’s intensity and the tight interplay of the rhythm section, even as they lament the audio quality.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviewers award 5‑star scores for the performance (especially The Seven), while the recording is repeatedly described as poor or muddy; weighting show quality (70 %) over audio (30 %) yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Maxell UD cassette tape with heavy hiss, missing/washed‑out vocals, bright but thin EQ, occasional drop‑outs; mix is decent for an audience source but organ buried and overall clarity low.

standout_songs: Doin' That Rag > The Seven > Good Lovin'
poor_songs: Good Lovin' (considered only so‑so by some reviewers)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers praise the seamless segues—especially the transition from Doin’ That Rag into The Seven and then into Good Lovin’. The jam is highlighted as a rare, full‑band moment that justifies the tape’s historic value.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Jerry's leads soaring through The Seven, describing his tone and improvisational fire as a key highlight.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as audible and “working it,” with Phil’s lines adding drive to the jam; some call his performance solid throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s guitar is said to shimmer front‑and‑center in the mix, especially during The Seven, giving him a prominent role.
band_member_comments.Keys: The organ/keyboard (TC) is reported as buried in tape hiss and not cutting through; overall keyboard presence is limited.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart receive high praise for “slicing and dicing,” tight synchronization, and near‑cheetah speed during the jam.
